title: Continuity of the Mills function away from zero
statement: For every nonzero real number $t$, the function $x\mapsto\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density, is continuous at $t$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, and define $F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by $F(0)=0$ and $F(x)=\varphi(x)(x^{-3}-x^{-1})$ for $x\ne0$. For every nonzero real $t$, the function $F$ is continuous at $t$.
